rv.q: When all the elements of the music come together, a triumphant feeling — call it uplift — charges the air.
Begin Again is a love letter to music, New York City, collaboration, and the strange, exhilarating act of creating something that did not exist five minutes ago.
Director Loren Latarro's production is smooth and lovely, ablaze in song and possessed of some choice bites of visual dazzle that give the production its dreaminess.
Act 1 is little more than cliched exposition, but once the two characters begin collaborating in Act 2, Begin Again gets a fresh start and delivers invigorating moments.
"Begin Again" the musical is a major improvement on its source material.
Bottom line, it's a feel-good show worth seeing, fun for the whole family.
Begin Again is an ultimately rousing tribute to the importance of authentic music that results in frequent applause.
Terrific music, performances, and sheer good feeling make this familiar story hard to resist.
The show may take itself a little too seriously – changing the world and all – but it’s a loveable journey and a fun watch.
Lorin Latarro ’s direction brings the emotional storytelling, movement, and music together into something cohesive and celebratory with humor and playfulness.
Her cohesive direction brought the various elements together, letting them work harmoniously and in parallel.
Jenna Clark Embry, Molly Beach Murphey, and Pat Monahan's new musical at the Old Globe is like riding a rollercoaster you may enjoy but have ridden many times before.

cn.t: This music-making musical hits familiar notes but charms with heart and strong performances. Critics find it a pleasant, tuneful confection that doesn't break new ground but captures the joy of creation.
